title: I shipped a turn-based mercenary game with AI. Lessons learned
author: ZeroFeels1
selftext:
Mercenary Charter just came out in Early Access on Steam. Turn-based tactics: you run a small mercenary company, take jobs from town boards and fight on a hex grid. Men die for good.



Solo dev. AI did a lot of the work, but nothing went in without me checking it.



What worked:

\- Generating whole scenes from scratch, picking the best of 3. Using one of my own scenes as a style reference kept hundreds of pieces consistent.

\- An AI coding assistant wrote most of the code, under strict rules: a test written first, a full test run before every build.

\- Checking every picture by eye. Automated checks caught a lot, but not everything.



What didn't:

\- Inpainting (patching old paintings). It cost hundreds of generations and kept giving cropped horses and merged legs. Repainting the whole scene was cheaper and better.

\- Letting the AI judge its own art. It once approved a horse with no legs.

\- Measuring the wrong thing. My job boards passed every test and still felt repetitive. The fix was more kinds of work, not more rules.



Happy to answer questions about the workflow.



[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5455440/Mercenary\_Charter/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5455440/Mercenary_Charter/)
